take_homes: The memory is a folder of my own text files. No extra licence, and a better model later reads the same folder. That undercuts my 'AI is a licence' view.
Make the agent show a plan before it acts and cite the file behind each claim, and keep it draft-only. Those are controls I can check.
It only knows what someone wrote down. Our month-end know-how sits in two heads, so that has to be written first.

monday.move: Ask my controller to put the last three month-end variance commentaries and the commentary template in a folder, and try the draft-only agent on one month with citations.
monday.who: Controller, with me reviewing the output
monday.stop_condition: Stop if the draft needs more correction than the controller's own draft would, or if IT says finance data can't go through the tool.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data, and nobody has told me the monthly cost per user.

misconception.why: The folder is plain text we own and the model can be swapped, so the asset is my team's files and not a licence. I still don't have a cost figure, so it's only shaken.

one_line: The folder-of-text part is the useful bit and I could check the citations, but I got no cost or payback number, and the styling and prework were wasted time.
